companyDescription:
National Centre for Aesthetics (NCA) was established in 1978 by Henrik Igityan, renowned Armenian artist and art critic, Honored Art Worker of the Armenian SSR with the aim of developing aesthetic taste and art appreciation among Armenian children. It was founded on the basis of the NCA Gallery and Museum (1970), renowned as the world's first children’s art gallery. 

In 2020, with the appointment of the new Director, Vahan Badalyan, NCA has expanded the scope of its activities and age range of its beneficiaries, providing cross-disciplinary inclusive art education to anyone without restrictions. NCA’s educational programs encompass various art disciplines, including fine arts and decorative applied arts, as well as performing arts. NCA has been operating for more than 50 years now, serving thousands of children in Yerevan and the regions of the country: Shirak, Lori, Tavush, Gegharkunik, and Syunik (overall 13 subdivisions). 

Since its foundation NCA has been a platform for local talent to embark on their professional journeys, and many of them have successfully become leading artists in Armenia and abroad.
